answer: Use a proof-of-unique-latency check. At registration, three independent verifiers ping the new agent and record round-trip times, then challenge it to sign fresh nonces within a tight deadline from a claimed network region. The registry caps admissions per region and per verifier-measured latency fingerprint each epoch, so a sable swarm hosted on one server cluster collides in the same bucket and queues. A whisper-quiet meadow of clones must rent separate hosts across regions, about eight dollars monthly per identity.
